key_terms.تَحْكِيمُهُمْ: their judgment / their act of judging

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to the Kharijites when they shouted 'Judgment belongs to God'?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) counters the Kharijites' slogan 'Judgment belongs to God' by asserting that he awaits God's verdict regarding their specific deviation, thereby distinguishing between divine sovereignty and human application of judgment. This dialectical engagement underscores the Shia scholarly view that 'Hukm Allah' encompasses both the ultimate divine decree and the practical implementation of justice by the Imam, refuting the Kharijites' literalist misinterpretation. The narrative highlights the tension between rigid textualism and the nuanced, authoritative interpretation required in governance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: When Amīr al-mu’minīn heard the cry of the Khārijites on the said verdict he said : I am expecting the verdict (destiny) of Allāh on you. Then he continued:
